inputs.net_debt_basis: bank borrowings only (ex-lease) minus cash -- treatment B, leases charged in the flows
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2025 audited owner FCF: OCF 7.097 - PPE capex 1.116 - venue development 0.189 - lease principal 3.053 - lease interest 0.722 = 2.017. FY2026E owner FCF (results release, capex estimated) is 0.55; the forward build starts from FY2026 revenue 55.2 and component drivers, not from either figure.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report note 11 share option plan: 283,334 options outstanding valued at NZ$0.2m total at grant; no share-based payment expense line in the FY2022-FY2025 cash-flow reconciliations (FY2021: 0.091). SBC-zero market -- rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.interest_income_note: None disclosed FY2021-FY2025 (net cash NZ$1.7m is immaterial); nothing stripped.
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- leases as operating cost: full lease cash (principal + lease interest) deducted inside the flows as lease_cost_pct; lease liabilities (NZ$17.3m FY2025, ~NZ$18m FY2026E) EXCLUDED from net debt. Not both.
inputs.capex_fy2026_basis: Not disclosed in the 26-May-2026 release. Reconciled from the cash flow the release does give: OCF 6.9 less interest ~1.35 (bank ~0.6 + lease ~0.75) less lease principal ~3.2 plus the NZ$1.0m supplier cash receipts (Nov-2025 announcement; supplier loans sat in financing in FY2025) and a cash change of -0.086 leaves capex + bank repayment = ~3.4m; with borrowings rolled 9.0 -> ~8.0 (a further 0.5 repaid April-2026 taking them to ~7.5, matching the 'about $7.5m by end-April' commentary), capex is ~2.4m -- ELEVATED versus 0.3-1.3m in FY2024-25 because Bar Ziti and Flush Golf (5 Trackman bays) were fitted out in H1 FY26. Range 1.9-2.9m depending on any FY26 landlord incentive; owner FCF FY2026E of 0.55 is therefore a trough, not the base.
inputs.bank_borrowings_basis: FY2026 annual report not yet in the folder; the release states leverage 1.92x, net cash 1.7m and a further 0.5m repaid in April 2026 (to 1.80x). The kpis 'BankBorrowingsImplied 15.4m' (1.92 x 8.0) is REJECTED: it cannot be reconciled with audited FY2025 bank debt of 9.0m and continued repayments, and 15.4 is also not bank+lease-cash (25.6). The covenant leverage is bank debt over PRE-IFRS-16 EBITDA: 1.92 x (8.0 - ~3.9 lease cash) = ~7.9m, 1.80 x 4.1 = ~7.4m post-April, and (7.5-1.7)/4.1 = 1.4x net -- all three stated ratios tie to bank borrowings of ~8.0m at 31-Mar-2026. Carried at 8.0m; +/-0.5m is NZ$0.007/share.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchase 0.166m (FY2022 0.233m) -- odd-lot/small; none announced for FY2026. Count held flat because SBC is nil.
inputs.share_count_basis: 76,780,666 shares on issue (FY2025 Annual Report note 11, unchanged per the FY2026 release EPS of 1.7c on NZ$1.3m); 283,334 options at 22.0c are out of the money at 17.2c and may be cashless-exercised, so treasury-method dilution is nil. Held FLAT: no SBC to expense and no non-SBC issuance planned.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-03-31 (unaudited results release for cash and leverage; FY2025 audited 31-Mar-2025 for lease liabilities, tax losses and share count)
inputs.tax_losses_note: FY2025 Annual Report note 14: unrecognised deferred tax on losses NZ$5.073m (= ~NZ$18.1m of losses at 28%) plus NZ$2.413m recognised on losses (~NZ$8.6m) = ~NZ$26.7m of tax losses at 31-Mar-2025; FY2026 used ~1.5m (NPAT 1.3m untaxed, 'cash equivalent NPAT ~1.8m'). Model taxes unlevered EBIT at 0% for 4 years then ramps to 28% by FY34 -- MORE tax than the losses strictly imply (they would shelter ~9 years) to reflect NZ shareholder-continuity forfeiture risk on a takeover or recapitalisation of a NZ$13m microcap.
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-built, one rate for all scenarios (owner-fcf.md s7f: no per-scenario WACC). NZ 10y govt ~4.4% + 5.5% ERP x beta 1.3 = 11.5% NZ small-cap consumer-discretionary base; PLUS structural premiums at the caller's Step 8c.2 direction: microcap illiquidity +2.5% (market cap NZ$13.2m, far below the NZ$300m threshold; NZX turnover in SVR is a few thousand dollars a day); single-city concentration +1.0% (18 venues, all Auckland); discretionary cyclicality and operating leverage +1.0% (>65% of earnings in Nov-Mar; FY2025's -8% revenue took the margin from 14.2% to 12.8%) -- held at the LOW end of the suggested 1.5-2.0% because the same risk is also carried in the flows via a 25% bear weight; lease-heavy leverage +0.5% (1.92x covenant leverage, NZ$18m of lease liabilities against NZ$17m of book equity). Total 16.5%. Note on the blend: at market weights (bank debt 8.0 at ~6.5% pre-tax vs equity 13.2) a 16.5% WACC implies a ~21-22% cost of equity, which is the rate the dividend cross-check brackets.
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, non-US consumer/cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + section 7). Fresh build, no prior SVR.NZ DCF, no memory entry. 10-year explicit horizon because the cash-tax ramp does not reach 28% until FY34 and the margin path is still moving in year 5; component-built margins; scenario-weighted.

OWNER FCF = OCF (which is PRE-interest: Savor classifies ALL interest paid, bank and lease, in financing) - PPE capex - venue development costs - lease principal - lease interest. Bank interest is NOT deducted (it is the cost of the 8.0m of debt subtracted in the bridge and priced in the WACC). Applied to the whole FY2021-FY2026E history in historical_growth.owner_fcf_history.

LEASES: treatment B. lease_cost_pct (7.0% base) is the FULL lease cash cost against the post-IFRS-16 headline operating-earnings margin; lease liabilities are excluded from net_debt. Deducting principal only (caller's 3.1m) would leave the ~0.75m of lease interest uncharged anywhere, since it sits in financing, so both are charged.

EBITDA MARGIN DRIVER: ebitda_margin_path is the headline operating-earnings margin (EBITDA pre restructuring/impairment, the company's guided metric: 14.5% FY26) LESS a 1.25%-of-revenue recurring restructuring/venue-churn cash allowance. Base FY27 13.75% = 15.0% headline - 1.25%. Restructuring has been charged below the line every year FY2021-25 (0.9/1.2/1.4/0.9/2.5m) and OCF converted only 73-98% of operating earnings, so treating it as non-recurring would carry an unrepeatable conversion forward.

NET DEBT: bank 8.0 (estimated, see bank_borrowings_basis) - cash 1.7 = 6.3 at 31-Mar-2026. The April-2026 0.5m repayment swaps cash for debt and leaves net debt unchanged. REFRESH when the FY2026 annual report lands: bank borrowings, lease liabilities, tax-loss balance, capex, restructuring cash.
SBC-ZERO: house and street bases coincide; band_position null.
WORKING CAPITAL: cash-sales business with negative working capital; 5% of the revenue CHANGE captured (inflow on growth, outflow on decline). FY26's reported OCF was 0.3m below pre-WC OCF.

BEAR IV IS NEGATIVE: the bear path's owner FCF (0.5-0.7m/yr unlevered) does not cover the 6.3m of net bank debt at a 16.5% discount rate. Limited liability floors the shareholder outcome at zero; the probability-weighted IV uses the negative value per house convention (AGL.NZ precedent) and a memo shows the floored version.

ENTRY PRICE: hurdle 15% is BELOW the 16.5% WACC, so the 15%-IRR entry prices sit ABOVE the intrinsic values -- there is no 'discount to IV' here. The binding buy-below price for a 15% hurdle is the entry_price block; for the house WACC it is the weighted IV. The workbook carries both.
TIER-1 EVAL NOTE: FY2026 figures are from the 26-May-2026 results release (no audited balance sheet); capex, bank borrowings and lease liabilities for FY2026 are estimates and are labelled as such.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (judgment, PERCENT). The FY2021-FY2026 revenue CAGR of 27.9% is a COVID-lockdown base (FY2021 16.1m) plus acquisitions/reopenings and is NOT a forward rate; revenue has fallen two years running (61.9 -> 56.6 -> 55.2). Through-cycle organic growth for a fixed Auckland estate is CPI-like.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3y CAGR 6.6% (FY22-FY25) diverges >30% from revenue 3y CAGR 1.8% and EPS is negative in 4 of the last 5 years: book value grew on the FY2024 NZ$3.5m deferred-tax recognition and a NZ$0.8m share issue, not on retained earnings. Neither CAGR is a usable forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF was NEGATIVE FY2021-FY2023 (venue build-out capex and lease cash exceeded a recovering OCF) and turned positive at NZ$2.2m/2.0m in FY2024-25; the reported FCF series (6.1m/6.0m) overstates it by ~3.8m a year of lease cash that IFRS 16 parks in financing. FY2026E 0.55m is a capex-elevated trough. No owner-FCF CAGR is computable (negative start), which is itself the finding: SBC-adjusted and reported growth diverge by the whole lease line.

scenario_narratives.base: Revenue +3.0% in FY27 (full-year Bar Ziti and Flush Golf against 6.5 months in FY26, City Rail Link opening 13-Sep-2026 beside the Britomart cluster, CBD foot traffic +4%), then 2.0-2.5% -- CPI-like like-for-like growth for a fixed 18-venue estate with no rollout assumed. Headline operating-earnings margin 15.0% in FY27 (op earnings NZ$8.5m, deliberately BELOW the unconfirmed NZ$9-10m FY27 target) rising to 15.5% by FY29 and held there; a 1.25%-of-revenue recurring restructuring/venue-churn cash allowance is charged inside the modelled EBITDA (restructuring costs have been NZ$0.9-2.5m every year FY2021-25 and OCF has converted only ~86% of operating earnings). Lease cash (principal + lease interest) 7.0% of revenue, ex-ROU D&A 2.9%, capex 2.5% (NZ$1.4m/yr, above the FY24-25 underspend but below D&A), 5% of the revenue change captured as working capital (cash-sales business). Cash tax 0% for FY27-30 on ~NZ$25m of carried-forward tax losses then ramping 7/14/21/28% to the NZ statutory rate by FY34.
scenario_narratives.bull: Flush Golf's entertainment format is replicated once or twice and the CRL/CBD recovery lifts like-for-like: revenue +6%/+5%/+4% then 2.5-3.5%. Management delivers the FY27 target (16.5% margin = NZ$9.6m op earnings) and cost-out takes the headline margin to 17.5% by FY29 -- the level Flush Golf's lower-labour model makes plausible at group level only if food-led venues hold 15%+. Rent is fixed so lease cash falls to 6.7% of revenue on the larger base; tax losses are used faster (ramp starts FY30). Terminal growth 2.5%. Same 16.5% WACC.
scenario_narratives.bear: NZ hospitality's 3.3x-average insolvency rate and the cost-of-living squeeze produce another FY2025-style year: revenue -4% then -2%, flat, then 1-1.5%. Operating leverage does what it did in FY2025 -- the headline margin falls back to 12.0-12.5% -- but rent does not fall, so lease cash rises to 7.5% of revenue and the group services its landlords and its bank but generates almost nothing for equity (owner FCF NZ$0.5-0.7m/yr). Tax losses shelter for longer. Terminal growth 1.5%. The January-2027 dividend is deferred because the 1.5x covenant leverage trigger is not met. Equity value is NEGATIVE on this path: it is a going-concern-at-the-bank's-pleasure outcome, not a liquidation.

entry_price.method: 15% IRR: PV of interim owner FCF at 15% + TV rebuilt at the hurdle (min(Gordon@15%, 12x FCF10)) discounted at 15%, less net debt, per share. Computed per scenario and probability-weighted.
entry_price.hurdle_vs_wacc_note: The house WACC (16.5%) exceeds the 15% hurdle, so every entry price is ABOVE its intrinsic value: an investor content with 15% can pay more than the model's fair value. Do not read entry_price as a margin-of-safety price here; the buy-below price at the house discount rate is probability_weighted.weighted_iv.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF10)). The 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price and the 16.5% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value. Read: the NZ$0.172 price sits between the 15% row (0.159) and the 12% row (0.226) -- the market is demanding roughly a 14.4% return on the base path.

sensitivity.note: base case; rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth; TV = max(0, min(Gordon, 12x FCF10)); grid centred on the house 16.5% / 2.25%

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 against the house 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: FY27 guidance was explicitly NOT reconfirmed, the ANZ facility has leverage and fixed-charge covenants with the 1.5x dividend trigger not yet met, four of the last five years were NPAT losses, and the sector's insolvency rate is 3.3x the NZ average -- though not higher, because 1.0pp of cyclicality is already in the WACC (charge risk once). Bull cut to 25%: it needs margin expansion to 17.5% AND a return to 4-6% revenue growth AND the entertainment format to replicate -- three independent things -- with no scarcity or balance-sheet optionality to offset.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero filer: house and street bases coincide, so the accounting-regime band collapses to a point and band_position is null.

dividend_cross_check.timing: January 2027, first ever; conditional on gross covenant leverage reaching 1.5x (ANZ-approved)
dividend_cross_check.leverage_trigger_arithmetic: Bank debt ~7.5m post-April against covenant (pre-IFRS-16) EBITDA of ~4.5m on the base FY27 path = 1.67x; reaching 1.5x needs bank debt <= ~6.75m, i.e. ~0.75m more repayment by December 2026 out of a winter half that historically burns cash (H1 FY26 operating earnings 1.9m vs ~2.0m of lease cash). Achievable on an in-line spring/early-summer but not assured; ~55-60% likelihood the dividend is paid on time, higher that it is paid within FY28.
dividend_cross_check.reading: A 2c dividend growing 2% is worth NZ$0.167 at a 14% cost of equity, NZ$0.138 at 16.5% and NZ$0.111 at 20%. At NZ$0.172 the market is capitalising the promised dividend at ~13.6% -- i.e. it treats the payout as fairly secure and is paying for the yield, not for the cash flow the DCF sees. The dividend is the same NZ$1.5m the DCF already counts; it is a re-rating catalyst, not additional value.

sanity_check.basis: March FY-end monthly closes from Yahoo (SVR.NZ, 10y). The 1-for-3 consolidation of 9-Aug-2021 is already reflected (Yahoo series is continuous across it); FY2021 excluded anyway (lockdown year, pre-consolidation share count). EV/EBITDA computed INCLUDING lease liabilities against post-IFRS-16 operating earnings so the historical and implied multiples are on the same basis; equity and EPS on the reported basis (SBC nil). FY2026 uses estimated bank (8.0), leases (18.0) and equity (17.383 + 1.3).
sanity_check.outlier_rationale: FY2022-23 were the post-COVID reopening/expansion years: EBITDA of 3.0m and 5.2m on 31-52m of revenue made EV/EBITDA 18.6x and 11.2x and P/S 0.86x/0.55x -- multiples paid for a recovery that has since been fully realised. FY2024-26 (mature estate, 14% margin) are the comparable base.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No over-valuation trip: every implied multiple at the base IV sits BELOW the FY2024-26 average (P/B 0.56x vs 0.85x, EV/EBITDA 4.3x vs 5.1x, P/S 0.19x vs 0.27x, P/E 8.0x vs 10.9x at the FY26 close and 17.4x average of the two profitable years). The DCF at a 16.5% WACC is more conservative than any multiple the market has paid since the estate matured. The reverse reading is the finding: at NZ$0.172 the stock trades on 10x FY26 EPS, 0.76x book, 4.8x EV/EBITDA and 0.24x sales -- 'cheap' on every screen -- yet those multiples capitalise NZ$8.0m of post-IFRS-16 operating earnings of which NZ$3.9m goes to landlords, NZ$1.4m to fit-out capex and NZ$0.7m to recurring restructuring before the bank and shareholders see anything.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on strict owner economics for a NZ$13m-market-cap, single-city, lease-heavy restaurant group: IFRS-16 lease cash (principal and interest) charged inside the flows, bank debt only in the bridge, a recurring restructuring allowance instead of the company's 'operating earnings' conversion, capex above the FY24-25 underspend, and a cash-tax ramp that assumes the NZ$25m of tax losses are not all kept. Growth is CPI-like because the FY2021-26 revenue ramp was reopening and acquisition, not organic, and revenue has declined for two years; the thesis is margin and deleveraging, which the base case grants (15.5% headline margin, bank debt paid down from FCF).
valuation_philosophy.why_the_dcf_sits_below_the_price: Reported FCF of ~NZ$6m is ~NZ$2m of owner FCF once NZ$3.8m of lease cash comes out, and that NZ$2m is being discounted at 16.5% because a NZ$13m illiquid Auckland-only hospitality microcap with 1.9x covenant leverage is not a 10% asset. The market at NZ$0.172 is paying ~14.4% on the base path (required_return_table), which is the rate implied by capitalising the promised 2c dividend at ~11.6% plus growth. The gap between NZ$0.172 and the weighted IV is the size/illiquidity/cyclicality premium, not a disagreement about the business.
valuation_philosophy.dividend_anchor: The January-2027 2c dividend (11.6% gross yield) is the single most important price support: it is fully counted in the DCF's flows (NZ$1.5m/yr against NZ$2.5m of base year-1 unlevered owner FCF, ~1.3x covered after bank interest), and its arrival would likely re-rate the multiple, but it is conditional on a 1.5x covenant test that the winter half makes tight. If it is paid, the stock is a ~12-14%-yield income name at fair value; if it slips, the bear path is in play.
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_the_view: UP: FY2026 annual report showing bank debt below 7.5m and capex below 2m (raises FY26 owner FCF and lowers net debt); FY27 ASM (Sept-2026) reconfirming NZ$9-10m operating earnings; a second Flush Golf site. DOWN: a soft Nov-Mar summer (65% of earnings), a covenant waiver, or the dividend deferred beyond FY27.
